initiative.title: Video to canvas
initiative.summary: Turn a narrated screen recording into a spatial, source-linked canvas reviewed in the portable HTML viewer; storyboard first, verified scroll joining second.
initiative.next_action: M5: Byron uses Canvas mode on his own sessions and records go/narrow/stop

sources.anchor: First proof; Repository fit; Decide whether to continue

sources.location: OpenCV motion API, FFmpeg showinfo, opencv-python-headless 4.14.0.94, scrollsnap

claims.statement: A narrated recording becomes a canvas explored in space, with every part linked back to its source video moment.
Displayed pixels come from real frames at known times; unobserved areas are never filled and different moments are never blended across text.
Primary case is a narrated product walkthrough over scrolling static content; lecture is second; general video is a research question.
Changed states sit to the right, frequent changes collapse into stacks, motion plays in place, returns are linked, narration sits near its visit, and large regions can be captured.
First version needs no browser instrumentation, cloud service, or new frontend stack; analysis is offline and on request.
The canvas must beat ordinary video and a change-selected storyboard on real tasks, or the simpler view wins.
The portable HTML viewer is the first surface; native SwiftUI waits for proven value.
process_session.py already embeds session data into viewer.html via write_viewer and uses ffmpeg/ffprobe.
Mark images and browser event offsets are not exact frame-exposure times; extract_frame discards actual output time.
No test suite or tracked sample recording; OpenCV is not installed locally; FFmpeg is.
The first canvas surface is the native Sessions window, not viewer.html.
Lead job: find content passed through faster than scrubbing; sole user is Byron.
First slice: tall column per scrolled page left to right; changes, returns, and motion are plain cards. Recordings under 5 minutes. Built on request.
First version includes copy/export of a column PNG and adding a review mark from canvas content; narration uses the existing now strip and inspector; continuation decided by personal use.

shape.appetite: Experiment-sized slice for recordings under 5 minutes in the native Sessions window; enough for Byron to judge from own use whether spatial review beats scrubbing.
shape.problem: Ordinary video review hides how much content was traversed, where it changed, and what was said about it.

recommended_shape.summary: Canvas stage mode in the Sessions window, built on request with one manual content box: storyboard cards first, then tall verified columns, with click-to-video, hover narration via existing now strip, column PNG export, and mark-from-canvas.

success_moves: Ship the storyboard in Canvas mode first; it is the refusal fallback and a useful result if stitching fails.
Develop joining against synthetic scroll clips cut from tall screenshots with FFmpeg so every offset is known exactly.
Burn a frame counter into synthetic clips to verify click-to-video lands on the true source frame.
Keep canvas.json + canvas/ as the single engine-neutral seam read by SessionModel; absent or mismatched data leaves the Sessions window unchanged.
Decide Python+OpenCV vs Apple Vision with one bake-off on the same fixtures, then keep only one engine.
Reuse RegionPicker, SessionModel.seek, NowStrip, and addReviewShot instead of new UI paths.

first_proof.question: Can verified joining reconstruct scrolled content with zero false joins, and do scripted walkthroughs produce readable columns that click back to the right frame?
first_proof.artifact: Synthetic fixture suite plus 2-3 scripted recordings under 5 minutes in Canvas mode.
first_proof.decision_rule: Use it on own sessions if synthetic p95 <= 2 px with zero false joins and scripted clips yield readable columns; otherwise keep the storyboard and stop stitching.

milestones.title: Storyboard in Canvas mode
milestones.outcome: Build canvas + content box produce change cards in a Canvas stage mode; click returns to video at the exact frame.
milestones.proof: Burned-in counter matches card frame after click; synthetic change clip yields expected cards.
milestones.valid_intermediate_state: Useful storyboard; sessions without canvas unchanged.
evidence: canvas-tool check: 10/10 fixture clips pass incl. barcode seek checks; real 97 s session -> 38 cards in 2.2 s; app build path via --build-canvas hook

milestones.title: Engine choice and joining on fake clips
milestones.outcome: One engine chosen; joins verified or refused with reasons.
milestones.proof: Fixture suite: p95 <= 2 px, zero false joins, refusal on every jump/edit fixture.
milestones.valid_intermediate_state: Storyboard still works; joining validated offline.
evidence: canvas-tool check: 10/10 clips pass with joining (p95 0 px, no false joins, refusals on jump/repeated/blank); bake-off in spikes/engine-bakeoff.md; real 97 s session -> 20 columns (max 8867 px) + 17 cards in 4.7 s

milestones.title: Tall columns in Canvas mode
milestones.outcome: Scripted clips show readable columns with cards between; every point clicks to its source frame.
milestones.proof: Click-to-frame spot checks and seam inspection.
milestones.valid_intermediate_state: Canvas usable on short real recordings.
evidence: canvas-tool check row->frame mapping 100% of sampled rows on all fixture columns; real 97 s session renders tall columns with hover time badge (offscreen render); scripted recordings by Byron still pending, real sessions used instead

milestones.title: Export a column and mark from the canvas
milestones.outcome: Columns copy/export as PNG; canvas selection creates a normal review mark.
milestones.proof: Mark time and crop match selection and survive reprocess.
evidence: canvas-tool check: canvas->video region mapping correct on all fixture columns (mutation-tested); real column selection produced review mark 8 whose shot matches the column crop (mean abs diff 0.16)

milestones.title: Decide from real use
milestones.outcome: Go/narrow/stop decision recorded from own sessions.
milestones.proof: Written judgment in the initiative map.

history.change: Prior research (intent brief, Pro report, design, proof plan, review) moved from docs/research/video-to-canvas to sources/ and reconciled into a sleuth intent brief.
Reordered proof: storyboard first as baseline and fallback; synthetic ground-truth clips before real footage.
Four milestones with one new dependency (OpenCV) isolated in M2 and a go/no-go in M4.

Three question rounds moved the surface to the native Sessions window (Canvas stage mode), set scope to <5 min recordings on request, added column PNG export and mark-from-canvas, replaced timed comparison with personal-use judgment, and added an engine bake-off.

M1 built: CanvasKit (AVFoundation decode with exact PTS, storyboard tracker, canvas.json), canvas-tool fixtures/check, Canvas stage mode. Analyzer moved from planned Python/FFmpeg to Swift because the project Python is stdlib-only.

M2: bake-off chose the in-app row-profile estimator (100% exact, 3.9 ms/pair, ambiguity signal, no dependency) over Vision (99.7%, 416 px miss) and OpenCV (100%, 25 ms, 50 MB dep). Added sub-pixel-tolerant verification and sticky-sidebar cropping from real footage.
M3: columns in Canvas mode with a hover time badge; row-to-frame mapping check added to canvas-tool. Purpose-made scripted recordings not yet recorded; existing real sessions stood in.
M4: Copy Image / Export PNG on canvas items; M and S marks from the canvas through the existing review-mark path; region math in CanvasItem.sourceRegion, checked against fixture truth.
